title: Boosting entrepreneurial intentions: A novel EEG-guided protocol
author: Patra, Mishra

steps.title: Classify participants
steps.instruction: Use a questionnaire survey to assign each participant to either the control group (significant entrepreneurial motivation/intention) or the study group (no significant entrepreneurial motivation/intention).

steps.title: Inform participants of session details
steps.instruction: Notify participants of the recording date, time, and location; require them to arrive at the recording studio at least 30 minutes before the scheduled start and to avoid any food or beverages with psychoactive effects for at least three hours prior to recording.

steps.title: Obtain informed consent and screen health
steps.instruction: Have participants sign a consent form confirming they have no history of mental illness, agree that administrators are not liable for medical problems, and understand that the EEG test is non‑invasive, painless, and does not require professional medical supervision. Disqualify any participant with a relevant mental‑health history.

steps.title: Prepare participant head
steps.instruction: Instruct participants the day before recording to wash their hair and abstain from alcohol and caffeine for at least eight hours. On arrival, measure head dimensions to determine electrode placement sites.

substeps.instruction: Instruct hair wash and 8‑hour alcohol/caffeine abstinence the day before.
Measure head circumference and landmarks for electrode positioning.

steps.title: Pre‑recording relaxation
steps.instruction: Invite the participant to sit at the recording station and relax for a minimum of 10 to 15 minutes to create a tranquil baseline condition.

steps.title: Record EEG signals
steps.instruction: Fit the participant with an 8‑ or 16‑channel wireless EEG cap, verify the wireless dongle connection, and record continuous EEG data for 5 to 10 minutes per session.

substeps.instruction: Attach the EEG cap according to the measured head landmarks.
Confirm wireless connection via the dongle.
Start recording and continue for 5–10 minutes.

steps.title: Verify participant safety
steps.instruction: After recording, confirm that the participant experienced no pain or discomfort during or after the session.

steps.title: Analyze EEG outcomes
steps.instruction: Compare the EEG outputs of the control and study groups; if the inter‑group differences are significantly reduced, conclude that the tested pedagogies increased entrepreneurial intentions in previously unmotivated individuals.
